markingScheme.criterion: Quotes two of their own Slicing Bench slices from the Investigation Record, each with the unit fraction divided, the whole number divided by and the resulting fraction of the whole bar (e.g. 'I cut ¼ into 3 and each piece was 1/12').
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine slices from the student's own Record with the correct result; exact wording not required. Records from the Photo Lab or Factory Dials stations are also accepted if the result is correct.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general statement ('I cut the chocolate and the pieces were small') with no figures from their own Record.

markingScheme.criterion: States the rule: to divide a unit fraction by a whole number, multiply the denominator by the whole number (the numerator stays 1), e.g. 1/n ÷ k = 1/(n × k). Alternatively states that the whole bar is split into n × k equal tiles.
markingScheme.accept: 'Multiply the bottom number by the number you divide by', 'count how many tiny pieces make the whole bar' or 'times the denominators' (treating the whole number as k/1 or as multiplying by 1/k). Equivalent wording accepted.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying the answer gets 'a different number' or 'a bigger denominator' without saying it is multiplied by the whole number.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why the pieces get smaller: sharing a piece among more parts (dividing by a whole number greater than 1) makes each part a smaller share of the whole, because the whole is now cut into more equal pieces (a bigger denominator).
markingScheme.accept: Any clear link between more equal parts and smaller parts, e.g. 'the more you cut it, the smaller each bit' or 'a bigger denominator means smaller pieces'.
markingScheme.insufficient: Restating that the answer is smaller without giving a reason.

markingScheme.criterion: Finds the correct answer: each friend gets 1/6 of the whole pizza.
markingScheme.accept: 1/6, ⅙, 'one sixth'. An unsimplified equivalent such as 2/12 is accepted.

markingScheme.criterion: Shows a valid method: ½ ÷ 3 = 1/(2 × 3) = 1/6, or draws/describes the pizza cut so that each half is split into 3 slices, giving 6 equal slices in the whole pizza, or writes ½ × ⅓.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct method: multiply the denominator by 3, a diagram of 6 slices, or ½ × ⅓ = 1/6.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating 1/6 with no method or diagram at all.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why each friend gets less than ½: because the half is shared among 3 people, each person's share is only one of three equal parts of the half, so it must be smaller than the half.
markingScheme.accept: Any reasoning linking sharing/dividing the half by 3 (more parts) to a smaller share, e.g. 'each person gets a third of the half, which is less than the half'.
markingScheme.insufficient: Restating that 1/6 is smaller than 1/2 without saying why.

markingInstructions: Mark the Explain and Apply answers using the analytic marking schemes above, one point at a time. Accept mathematically valid alternative wording and any correct method. The Explain marks feed 'Use of the Investigation Record' and the Apply marks feed 'Mathematical reasoning'; 'Communication' is judged holistically across both answers and never re-awards content marks. Do not penalise spelling or grammar unless the meaning is unclear. Check quoted figures against the Investigation Record table. Return: total score, score by criterion, one strength, one correction, one next step. Keep feedback under 80 words.
